content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper presents an affinity-VAE for automatic clustering and classification of objects in multidimensional image data based on their similarity. The main contribution, compared with beta-VAE, is a similarity regularization term.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. The motivation is clearly presented, and the idea of this paper is easy to follow.
2. The visual experiment of this paper is comprehensive and it verifies the effectiveness of Affinity-VAE to some extent.

Weakness:
1. The contribution of this paper is limited. The difference between Affinity-VAE and $\beta$-VAE is only the affinity-based loss, which is quite heuristic.
2. How does the pose feature space influence the clustering and classification performance of Affinity-VAE? There is also no corresponding discussion in the paper.
3. The experimental setup was not described in detail, which limits the reproducibility of the proposed method.
4. The paper lacks statistical experimental analysis. The performance of Affinity-VAE in terms of some widely used metrics (e.g. NMI, ARI for clustering task and Accuracy for classification task) should be provided.
5. The paper lacks comparison experiment. The authors only compare it with $\beta$-VAE. The effectiveness of the proposed Affinity-VAE should be verified via comparing it with state-of-the-art of deep clustering.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The clarity and quality should be improved carefully. The novelty is limited and below the bar of accepted papers in ICLR. The paper lacks comparison with state-of-the-art of clustering methods, which makes reproducibility meaningless.
content.summary_of_the_review: In sum, the quality of the paper is much lower than the bar of ICLR.

content.confidence: 2: You are willing to defend your assessment, but it is quite likely that you did not understand the central parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes a new model in the Variational AutoEncoder (VAE) family. It extends beta-VAE with an additional loss term that encourages latent representations to have a high/low inner product according to a given affinity matrix that indicates a prior on the similarity of each pair of samples. This loss term is controlled by an additional hyperparameter lambda that weighs it against the rest of the VAE terms. The authors show encouraging results in interpretability and disentangling of the latent representations.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Strengths:**

[+] Adding a loss term to encourage latent representations to be close if the samples are similar is intuitive and can help learn better representations.

**Weaknesses:**

[-] However, the method requires a pairwise affinity matrix, which requires prior knowledge about the task and might make it unfeasible when such knowledge is not known a priori or we are dealing with a large number of samples.
[-] In practice, the results are not that different from the baseline, and novel methods to learn representations that are based in optimizing distances of sample representations have been proposed with great success (contrastive learning methods), reducing the impact of this method.
[-] For the same reason as above (existing contrastive methods), the novelty of the method is limited.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
* Clarity: the paper is clearly written and presented.

* Quality: the method is well motivated and explained, the experimental section is relatively simple but correct.

* Novelty: the paper has low novelty in light of previous constrastive and VAE methods.

* Reproducibility: the paper includes enough details to be reproducible.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper presents an extension of VAEs with a term that encourages latent representations to be close/far depending on a precomputed similarity matrix. This matrix might not be available for all domains and can be quite expensive to use when using large datasets. Furthermore, this loss term is quite similar to training objectives used by constrastive learning methods. Overall, the novelty of the paper is limited, and therefore my borderline rating.

content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
The authors propose a novel method called affinity-VAE and use it for analyzing image data.

Weaknesses
The proposed affinity-VAE might not be novel.

content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The idea of utilizing similarities in training VAE might not be novel. A similar idea has been previously proposed [1, 2]. The authors do not discuss why they choose the specific design of the model and why it is better than these existing methods. The authors also do not compare affinity-VAE with these methods in the experiments.

The authors report some experimental results and compare affinity-VAE with beta-VAE. However, limited quantitative results are provided. It is not obvious whether affinity-VAE outperforms beta-VAE.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes a new model called affinity-VAE for clustering objects in images. The proposed method builds over beta-VAE by adding a loss term that encourages the learned representations to have similar affinity values as a predetermined affinity matrix. Affinity-VAE also includes an additional encoder component to encode the pose information of the objects. The experiments present clustering results for 3 datasets — 2D alpha-numeric data, 3D tetrominoes and 3D simulated protein data. The results show reasonable clustering for all datasets, visually interpretable interpolations in latent dimensions, and contrast the proposed affinity-VAE with beta-VAE. The experiments also include results that show the influence of the hyperparameter and the choice of similarity function in the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
- The proposed affinity-based criterion can be useful in controlling the structure of the representation space. 
- Experiments on three different datasets spanning 2D and 3D domains help in evaluating the robustness of the proposed method.
- The paper focuses on real scientific data and applications. 


Weaknesses:

- My biggest concern is the experimental results. 
    - Sections 3.1-3.3 present qualitative and subjective results without any comparative references. How do the presented results compare to other methods such as beta-VAE, vanilla VAE, representations from a trained classification network or even a randomly initialized neural network?
    - In Section 3.4, I would argue that the clustering for affinity-VAE is not better than that of beta-VAE. They are different and any one of them can be desirable based on the downstream task. The clustering for beta-VAE seems equally, if not more, separable by linear decision boundaries as compared to affinity-VAE. Also, it is not clear if the difference in the cluster shapes is because of the affinity-based criterion or the additional “pose” encoder. What about the case when there is affinity-based loss is used but the pose component is off? Also, normalizing the distances could be very sensitive to an outlier.
    - Again, the visualizations in Section 3.5 are subjective, there is no clear trend I can draw from them without a downstream task in mind.
- The introduction mentions several previous works — Moebel et al., 2021, Che et al., 2018, Min et al., 2015, Chen et al., 2020, Ji et al., 2017, etc. and their issues or how the proposed method is different from them. Does the proposed method overcome these issues such as the need of large amounts of data? How does the proposed method compare to these methods for the experimental settings in this paper?
- Could the authors explain Equation 3 in more detail? What is z_i here? Is it not the latent representation for a data instance x_i? How do the indices i and j relate to the classes?
- There are many design choices that are not explained well — how are the hyperparameters selected? How are the letters and numbers selected for the alphanumeric dataset? How are these symbols rendered in images? How many original samples are used in Figure 3?
- How can it be ensured that the additional encoder component actually encodes the pose?
- Minor: The visualizations in Figures 4 and 5 could be improved by using different symbols for train/val/test instead of opacity.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity - The paper is clearly written and easy to read. However, most of the design decisions are not supported with justifications, some of them are mentioned in weaknesses above.

Quality - The experimentation in the paper is of poor quality without significant comparisons and concrete evaluation metrics. Without this, it is hard to evaluate the quality of the proposed approach.

Novelty - The proposed approach seems to be novel. Its application to scientific problems is also an under-explored area.

Reproducibility - The paper leaves out a lot of experimental details, therefore the reproducibility of the proposed approach is low.
content.summary_of_the_review: I think there are major concerns about the experimentation and comparison with previous works, without which it is hard to evaluate the importance of the proposed approach. Hence, I recommend the paper for rejection.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.

content.title: Response to reviewers
content.comment:
Dear reviewers,


Thank you very much for the time and attention you've given to the review of our manuscript. We very much appreciate all the comments we can use to further evaluate and improve our proposed method.


While we already investigated some of the points raised as shortcomings since the submission, we are yet to perform extensive comparisons with existing methods, as suggested by the reviewers and for that reason we've decided to withdraw the paper. In future iterations of this work we will take into account the suggestions from the reviewers, including more rigorous and quantitative evaluation, comparison with other variants of VAEs as well as other deep subspace clustering and contrastive learning methods. In the next version of the manuscript we will demonstrate how the pose component together with affinity matrix can discourage sources of within-class variance out of the latent space thus improving class separability and factorisation in the latent space, consequently improving accuracy and emphasising the novelty and potential impact of the method.


Once again, we value all the suggestions and points raised by the reviewers and we would like to thank all reviewers for their time in evaluating our method.
